definition_zh: 评估；评定；评价；教育测评；核定（税额）；评估结果
definition_en: the act of judging the value, quality, or amount of something, a formal judgement, a test of learning, or a tax fixed by authority
core_image: 一叠批改过的作文与一支红笔，旁边写着定好的分数
scene: 学期末的办公桌上摊着一摞作文，红笔在每页的分数栏里落下数字。The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 assessment 是「评估、评定」（第 1 个义项：判断价值或质量的行为）；句意为「每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟」。画面中有摊开的作文、红笔与分数栏。

pos.zh: 名词：评估；评定；评价；教育测评；核定税额；评估结果

derivatives.zh: assessment 的动词形式，义为「评估；评定；核定」
由 assess 加 -or 构成，义为「评估员；估税员」
由 assess 加 -able 构成，义为「可评估的；可征税的」
由前缀 re- 加 assessment 构成，义为「重新评估」

senses.title: The act of judging value or quality
senses.definition: the act of judging or estimating the value, quality, or seriousness of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断或估算某物的价值、质量或严重程度的行为
senses.example: The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟。
senses.why: -ment turns the verb assess into the action itself: the sitting-beside and weighing is now a named event.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词 assess 变成动作本身：那场「坐在旁边称一称」如今成了一个有名字的事件。

senses.title: A test of learning
senses.definition: a formal test or judgement of a pupil's progress, often spread over a course
senses.definitionCN: 对学生学习进展的正式测评，常贯穿整个课程
senses.example: The course uses continuous assessment instead of one final exam.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课采用持续性评价，而不是一次期末考试。
senses.why: If weighing a pupil's work is assess, then the whole system of weighing is an assessment.
senses.whyCN: 如果评一份作业是 assess，那么整套称量的制度就是 assessment。

senses.title: A tax fixed by authority
senses.definition: an official calculation of the tax or fine owed by a person or property
senses.definitionCN: 对个人或财产应缴税款、罚金的官方计算
senses.example: The tax assessment arrived with the winter bill.
senses.exampleCN: 税额核定单随冬季账单一起寄到。
senses.why: This is the oldest official use: an assessor sits beside the property and names the sum.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的官方用法：估税员坐在产业旁边，报出一个数目。

senses.title: The judgement reached
senses.definition: the opinion or rating that results from assessing something
senses.definitionCN: 评估某物之后得出的意见或评级
senses.example: Her assessment was that the plan needed more time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的评价是这个计划还需要更多时间。
senses.why: By shifting from the act to its result, an assessment becomes the verdict someone has reached.
senses.whyCN: 由行为转指结果，assessment 便成了某人得出的结论。

intro.en: Assessment is the noun of assess, and both keep the Latin image of an official sitting beside a property to fix its value.
intro.cn: assessment 是 assess 的名词，两者都保留着「官员坐在产业旁边核定价值」这一拉丁意象。

items.en: The root 「*sed-」 meant 'to sit', and it lies behind many Latin words for sitting and settling.
items.cn: 词根「*sed-」意为「坐」，拉丁语中许多表示坐与安顿的词都由它而来。

items.en: Assidere meant 'to sit beside', from ad- 'to' plus sedere 'to sit'.
items.cn: assidere 意为「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sedere「坐」构成。

items.en: An assessor sat beside a magistrate to fix taxes and fines.
items.cn: assessor 坐在长官旁边，协助核定税额与罚金。

items.en: Assesser carried the verb into French with the sense of fixing what is owed.
items.cn: 古法语 assesser 把这个动词带进法语，意思是核定应缴数额。

items.en: English assess began with taxes, and assessment followed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语的 assess 先用于税务，assessment 随后作为它的名词出现。

items.en: Education gave the word a large new field: continuous assessment now weighs pupils, not property.
items.cn: 教育为这个词开辟了大片新领域：持续性评价如今称量的是学生，而非产业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns close to assessment in form; the near-meaning group gathers evaluations, appraisals and reviews.
note.cn: 形近组收形式上与 assessment 接近的名词；近义组收评估、鉴定与复查。

entries.definition: A person who assesses, especially one who values property for tax.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「评估员、估税员」。

entries.definition: A part cut off from a whole.
A confident statement that something is true.
A careful judgement of value or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值或质量的仔细判断。

entries.definition: A judgement of worth, often of property or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值的评估，常指房产或表现。

entries.definition: An opinion or decision formed after thought.
entries.definitionCN: 经过思考后形成的意见或决定。

entries.definition: An examination of something to judge its state or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 为判断状况或质量而进行的检查。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from marked essays to a school report, a tax notice and a spoken verdict.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从批改过的作文，走到成绩报告、税单与一句口头结论。

normal.en: Assessment is assess turned into a named event.
normal.cn: assessment 是把 assess 变成一个有名有姓的事件。

normal.en: An assessment of essays: each one is weighed.
normal.cn: 作文评估：每一篇都过一回秤。

normal.en: Continuous assessment: the weighing never stops.
normal.cn: 持续性评价：称量一直没停。

normal.en: A tax assessment: the property is weighed for what it owes.
normal.cn: 税额核定：产业被称一称，看它该缴多少。

normal.en: Her assessment was a verdict in one sentence.
normal.cn: 她的一句评价就是最终结论。

abstract.en: The noun names the act and then the verdict.
abstract.cn: 这个名词先指动作，再指结论。

abstract.en: Tax and school both use the same scale.
abstract.cn: 税务与学校用的是同一架天平。

abstract.en: Every assessment needs a standard to weigh against.
abstract.cn: 任何评估都需要一个可比照的标准。

examples.en: The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
examples.cn: 每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟。

examples.en: The course uses continuous assessment instead of one final exam.
examples.cn: 这门课采用持续性评价，而不是一次期末考试。

examples.en: Her assessment was that the plan needed more time.
examples.cn: 她的评价是这个计划还需要更多时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿塞斯门」——阿塞斯门坐在办公桌前，把每份作业都称一称、打个分：评估

root: assessment 是 assess 加名词后缀 -ment。assess 来自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」与 sedere「坐」构成；assessor 原是坐在长官旁边核定税额的官员。因此 assessment 先指「核定应缴数额」这一官方行为，后泛指判断价值、质量、风险的行为，再指教育中的测评制度，最后由行为转指得出的评价与结论。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses grow from one weighing: the act of judging, a course-wide test of learning, an official tax sum, and the verdict reached.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从同一次称量长出来：判断的行为、贯穿课程的测评、官方核定的税额，以及最终得出的结论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of marked essays beside a red pen and a column of scores.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠批改过的作文，旁边是一支红笔与一列分数。

branches.en: THE WEIGHING LINE: judging value or quality is the core act.
branches.cn: 称量线：判断价值或质量是核心动作。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: the weighing becomes a course-long system.
branches.cn: 学校线：称量变成贯穿课程的制度。

branches.en: THE TAX LINE: an official fixes what a property owes.
branches.cn: 税务线：官员定下产业该缴多少。

branches.en: THE VERDICT LINE: the act turns into the opinion reached.
branches.cn: 结论线：动作转成得出的意见。

branches.en: THE REPORT LINE: a written assessment records both the act and the verdict.
branches.cn: 报告线：书面评估同时记录动作与结论。

intro.en: Assessment is assess plus -ment; its family adds -or, -able and the prefix re-.
intro.cn: assessment 是 assess 加 -ment，词族再加 -or、-able 与前缀 re-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root sedere 'to sit' also gave assessor and sedentary, keeping the image of sitting beside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 sedere「坐」还生出 assessor 与 sedentary，保留着「坐在旁边」的形象。

items.meaning: to judge or fix a value

items.example: The city reassessed the flood risk.

items.meaning: judging one's own work or tax
items.meaningCN: 自我评估；自行申报纳税
items.example: Self-assessment saves the office a visit.

latinEntries.meaning: one who sits beside to judge
latinEntries.meaningCN: 坐在旁边协助判断的人
latinEntries.example: The assessor set the fine at ten pounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 估税员把罚金定为十英镑。

latinEntries.example: A sedentary life weakens the legs.

definition_en: something valuable that a person or company owns, or a useful quality
core_image: 账本左栏一件件能换成钱的东西
scene: 公司最值钱的不是机器，而是那批老客户。Her calm voice is a great asset in court.
sceneCN: 这里 asset 是「优势」（第 2 个义项：能带来好处的人或特质）；句意是她在法庭上沉稳的嗓音是一大优势。

senses.title: Property of value
senses.definition: something of value owned by a person or a company
senses.definitionCN: 个人或公司拥有的、有价之物
senses.example: The company sold several assets to pay its debts.
senses.exampleCN: 公司卖掉几项资产来还债。
senses.why: Asset comes from Norman French asetz, 'enough to settle a debt', so the word began as property counted for its ability to pay.
senses.whyCN: asset 来自诺曼法语 asetz，原指「足以清偿债务的财产」，所以这个词一开始就是按「能抵债」来计量的财物。

senses.title: Useful quality or person
senses.definition: a person or quality that is useful and brings benefit
senses.definitionCN: 有用、能带来好处的人或特质
senses.example: Her calm voice is a great asset in court.
senses.exampleCN: 她在法庭上沉稳的嗓音是一大优势。
senses.why: Once anything that can pay off is counted as an asset, the step to a helpful person or trait is short: both are reckoned by the benefit they bring.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能抵用、能带来回报的东西都被算作资产，再向前一步，能帮上忙的人或特质也就成了资产，衡量标准都是「带来多少好处」。

intro.en: Asset is a Norman French word about having enough, and English turned it into a noun for property.
intro.cn: asset 是来自诺曼法语的词，本义与「足够」有关，英语把它变成表示财产的名词。

items.en: ad satis meant 'to enough', enough to meet a claim.
items.cn: ad satis 意为「达到足够」，即足以应付索偿。

items.en: asez meant 'enough, sufficiency of wealth'.
items.cn: asez 意为「足够、财富充裕」。

items.en: asetz named the property left by a debtor, enough to pay.
items.cn: asetz 指债务人留下的、足以偿债的财产。

items.en: English took assets as a plural noun for property and funds.
items.cn: 英语以复数形式 assets 借入，指财产与资金。

items.en: The sense widened to any valuable quality or helpful person.
items.cn: 词义扩大，凡有价值的特质或能帮忙的人也算资产。

note.en: The look-alike group is spelled like asset; the near-meaning group names property and advantage.
note.cn: 形近组拼写与 asset 相近；近义组是表示财产与优势的词。

normalIntro.en: An asset is whatever can be counted on the left side of the ledger.
normalIntro.cn: 资产就是账本左栏里能数得出来的东西。

normal.en: The plural is far more common in finance: assets.
normal.cn: 在财务语境里复数形式更常见。

normal.en: It is a countable noun: a great asset, several assets.
normal.cn: 它是可数名词：一大优势、几项资产。

normal.en: One t in the middle, and stress falls on the first syllable: AS-set.
normal.cn: 中间只有一个 t，重音在第一个音节。

normal.en: The phrase be an asset to praises a person's value.
normal.cn: 短语 be an asset to 用来称赞某人的价值。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with assess, which is the verb.
normal.cn: 不要和动词 assess 混淆。

abstract.en: See a ledger page where each line can be turned into cash.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上每一行都能换成现金。

abstract.en: See a quiet colleague whose presence steadies a whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一位安静同事，他一来整个屋子就稳住了。

abstract.en: See a key that opens more than one door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能开不止一扇门的钥匙。

examples.en: The company sold several assets to pay its debts.
examples.cn: 公司卖掉几项资产来还债。

examples.en: Her calm voice is a great asset in court.
examples.cn: 她在法庭上沉稳的嗓音是一大优势。

examples.en: Patience is an asset when you learn a language.
examples.cn: 学语言时，耐心是一种优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 诺曼法语 asetz 本指「够还债的财产」，进入英语成 assets；从「能抵债的财物」引申为资产，再到「能帮忙的人或特质」。

root: 诺曼法语 asetz 意为「足以偿债的财产」，源自拉丁语 ad satis「达到足够」；由够还债的财物引申为资产，再抽象为能带来好处的优势。

sensesIntro.en: Property counted for what it can pay and a person counted for what they can give share one measure of value.
sensesIntro.cn: 财物按能抵多少债来算，人按能带来多少好处来算，用的是同一把价值尺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger line that can be turned into cash.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上一行可以换成现金的条目。

intro.en: Asset is a borrowed whole word, but it sits in a wide field of property and value terms.
intro.cn: asset 是整体借入的词，但它处在一大片表示财产与价值的词场中。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin ancestor ad satis, 'to enough', also underlies satisfy and satiate.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁语祖词 ad satis「达到足够」，也是 satisfy 与 satiate 的来源。

definition_zh: 分配；指派；确定（时间、地点）
definition_en: to give a task or share to someone, or to fix a time, place or right
core_image: 名册上每个名字旁边写着分到的那一份
scene: 编辑部的白板上写着各人负责的栏目。She was assigned to the travel desk.
sceneCN: 这里 assign 是「指派」（第 1 个义项：把任务分给某人）；句意是她被派去负责旅游版。

senses.title: Give a task or share
senses.definition: to give someone a particular job or a share of something
senses.definitionCN: 把某项工作或某一份东西交给某人
senses.example: She was assigned to the travel desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她被派去负责旅游版。
senses.why: Assign comes from Latin assignare 'to mark out', the act of noting on a list that a thing belongs to a certain person, so the sense is a marked allotment.
senses.whyCN: assign 源自拉丁语 assignare「作标记」，原指在名册上标明某物归谁，因此核心是「标好归属的分派」。

senses.title: Fix a time or place
senses.definition: to decide and state a time, place or value
senses.definitionCN: 确定并说明时间、地点或数值
senses.example: The judge assigned a date for the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 法官确定了听证日期。
senses.why: Marking on a list also served to pin down when and where something happens, so 'allot' extended to fixing a date or place.
senses.whyCN: 在名册上作标记同样用于给日子和地点定位，于是「分派」自然引申为把时间、地点确定下来。

senses.title: Transfer by law
senses.definition: to transfer property or a right to another person in law
senses.definitionCN: 依法把财产或权利转到他人名下
senses.example: He assigned the copyright to the publisher.
senses.exampleCN: 他把版权转让给了出版社。
senses.why: Writing a right under another person's name is the most literal form of the marking act, and law kept that concrete sense as 'transfer'.
senses.whyCN: 把一项权利登记到别人名下，是「作标记」最字面的一种做法，法律保留了这个具体含义，用作「转让」。

intro.en: Assign is a word about marking names, which English uses for tasks, dates and legal rights.
intro.cn: assign 本义是「标记名字」，英语用它来说任务、日期与法律权利。

latinIntro.en: Signum is Latin for a mark, and its family spread into law, art and language.
latinIntro.cn: signum 是拉丁语「记号」，这一族词进入了法律、艺术与语言领域。

definition_en: a piece of work given to someone, or the act of giving it out
core_image: 一张写好的任务纸被放到桌上
scene: 课代表把一摞纸发下来。The whole class groaned at the assignment.
sceneCN: 这里 assignment 是「作业」（第 1 个义项：布置下来的任务）；句意是全班看到作业都叹气。

senses.title: Work given to someone
senses.definition: a piece of work given to a person as part of their job or study
senses.definitionCN: 作为工作或学业的一部分分派给某人的活儿
senses.example: The whole class groaned at the assignment.
senses.exampleCN: 全班看到这份作业都叹气。
senses.why: Assignment is assign plus -ment, and this suffix turns the act of allotting into the thing allotted, so it names the work that lands on a person's desk.
senses.whyCN: assignment 是 assign 加 -ment，这个后缀把「分派」的动作变成被分派的东西，所以它指落到某人桌上的那份活。

senses.title: Act of allocating
senses.definition: the act of giving out duties, rights or property
senses.definitionCN: 把职责、权利或财产分出去的行为
senses.example: The assignment of seats took ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 分配座位花了十分钟。
senses.why: The same suffix can also name the action itself, so assignment keeps an abstract sense of the handing-out process.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也能指动作本身，因此 assignment 保留了「分发这一行为」的抽象义。

intro.en: Assignment is the noun built on assign, a word about marking a name on a list.
intro.cn: assignment 是由 assign 构成的名词，而 assign 本指在名册上标出名字。

items.en: signum meant 'a mark or sign'.
items.cn: signum 意为「标记、符号」。

items.en: assignare meant 'to mark out and allot'.
items.cn: assignare 意为「标出并分派」。

items.en: assigner carried the sense 'to allot or appoint'.
items.cn: assigner 表示「分派、指定」。

items.en: English assignen meant 'to allot or fix'.
items.cn: 英语 assignen 意为「分派、确定」。

items.en: The suffix -ment produced assignment, the task or the act of giving it.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 构成 assignment，指任务，也指分派这一行为。

note.en: The look-alike group is the assign family; the near-meaning group names work and duties.
note.cn: 形近组是 assign 词族；近义组是表示工作与职责的词。

normalIntro.cn: assignment 就是名字被标在旁边之后，出现在你桌上的那份东西。

normal.en: The verb is assign, the noun adds -ment.

normal.en: It covers both school work and tasks given at work.
normal.cn: 它既可指学校作业，也可指工作中的任务。

normal.en: On assignment means sent somewhere to do a job.

normal.en: The middle syllable carries the stress: as-SIGN-ment.

abstract.en: See a blank square on a calendar filled in by another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上的空格被别人的手填上。

abstract.en: See a desk lamp on at midnight over unfinished work.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜台灯下还没做完的活。

sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项是那份活本身，另一个义项是把活分出去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of work with a name written at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份写着名字的工作纸。

definition_zh: 吸收；同化；使相似；逐渐融入
definition_en: to take something in and make it part of a larger whole, or to become like that whole
core_image: 一块冰放进温水，边界一点点消失，最后整杯水都带着它的凉意
scene: 身体把一碗饭变成力气，学生把新公式接进旧知识，新来的邻居慢慢学会本地口音。It took the newcomer a decade to assimilate the local customs and speech.
sceneCN: 这里 assimilate 指「吸收并融入当地习俗与语言」（第 1 个义项：把外部事物纳入自身并使之一致）；句意为这个新来者花了十年才吸收并融入当地的习俗与说话方式。可辨识物件：饭碗、课本、街区门廊、口音示意。

pos.zh: 吸收（营养、知识）；使同化；使相似

senses.title: Absorb nutrients
senses.definition: to take food or a substance into the body and convert it into usable material
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或物质纳入身体并转化为可用物质
senses.example: The body assimilates iron more easily when vitamin C is present.
senses.exampleCN: 有维生素配合时，身体更容易吸收铁。
senses.why: The oldest concrete sense: the body makes foreign matter into its own substance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的具体义：身体把外来物质变成自身物质。

senses.title: Absorb and understand information
senses.definition: to take in ideas or information until they become part of one's understanding
senses.definitionCN: 把观念或信息纳入，使其成为理解的一部分
senses.example: Students need time to assimilate the new material before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 学生需要时间在考试前吸收新材料。
senses.why: The mind repeats the body's work: what is taken in must be broken down and rebuilt as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 心智重复身体的工作：纳入之物必须被拆解并重建为自己所有。

senses.title: Become part of a group or culture
senses.definition: to become absorbed into a community and take on its ways, often used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 被一个社群吸收并接受其生活方式，常不带宾语
senses.example: Many newcomers assimilate within a generation and keep little of the old tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 许多新来者在一代人之内融入，只留下很少的旧语言。
senses.why: Here the person is both the thing absorbed and the agent of change, which is why the verb can stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 这里的人既是被吸收之物，也是变化的行为者，因此这个动词可以单独使用。

senses.title: Make one thing like another
senses.definition: to make something resemble something else, often with 'to' in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 使某物与另一物相似，正式文体中常用介词引出比较对象
senses.example: The reform assimilates local practice to the national model.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革使本地做法向全国模式靠拢。
senses.why: This transitive pattern keeps the Latin frame: one thing is made like another, and the direction is explicit.
senses.whyCN: 这个及物结构保留拉丁框架：一物被弄得像另一物，方向明确。

senses.title: Assimilate a speech sound
senses.definition: to change a sound so that it becomes more like a neighbouring sound
senses.definitionCN: 改变一个语音，使其更接近相邻语音
senses.example: In rapid speech, speakers assimilate the final nasal to the following consonant.
senses.exampleCN: 在快速语流中，说话人让词尾鼻音向后续辅音同化。
senses.why: Sounds are the smallest things that can be absorbed: one phoneme borrows a feature from its neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 语音是可以被吸收的最小事物：一个音位从邻居借来一个特征。

senses.title: Absorb into an organization
senses.definition: to merge a smaller unit into a larger structure so that it operates as part of it
senses.definitionCN: 把较小单位并入较大结构，使其作为其中一部分运作
senses.example: The agency assimilated the smaller office into its own structure.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构把较小的办事处并入自己的架构。
senses.why: Institutions use the verb for mergers, because a merged unit is expected to adopt the parent's procedures.
senses.whyCN: 机构用这个动词指合并，因为被并入的单位被期望采用母体的程序。

senses.title: Digest an experience
senses.definition: to process a difficult experience until it can be understood and carried
senses.definitionCN: 处理艰难经历，直到它能被理解并承受
senses.example: Children assimilate difficult events through play and repeated stories.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童通过游戏与反复讲述来消化艰难事件。
senses.why: The psychological sense treats experience as food: it must be taken in slowly before it can nourish.
senses.whyCN: 心理义把经验当作食物：必须慢慢纳入，才能滋养人。

senses.title: Absorb a people or territory by force
senses.definition: to bring a people or region under control and erase its separate identity
senses.definitionCN: 把民族或地区纳入控制并抹去其独立身份
senses.example: The empire assimilated the border province over several decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国用几十年时间吞并了边境省份。
senses.why: Power uses the same word as digestion: to assimilate a people is to consume them as a body consumes food.
senses.whyCN: 权力使用与消化相同的词：同化一个民族，就是像身体消化食物那样吞并它。

intro.en: Assimilate comes from Latin assimilare 'to make like, to absorb', from ad- 'to' and similis 'like'. It entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: assimilate 来自拉丁 assimilare「使相似、吸收」，由 ad-「向」与 similis「相似」构成，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Similis meant 'like, similar'. It is generally connected with simul 'together', but the pre-Latin shape is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: similis 意为「相似的」。一般认为与 simul「一起」同源，但拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式，并无实际书证。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus similis gave assimilare 'to make like, to liken, to absorb'.
items.cn: ad-「向、朝」加 similis 构成 assimilare「使相似、比作、吸收」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the sixteenth century through French, first meaning 'to make similar'.
items.cn: 这个动词在十六世纪经法语进入英语，最初意为「使相似」。

items.en: Physiology applied it to food becoming tissue, and psychology to new experience becoming part of a schema.
items.cn: 生理学用它指食物变成组织，心理学用它指新经验成为图式的一部分。

items.en: Modern sociology uses it for newcomers becoming like a host society, and linguistics for neighbouring sounds becoming alike.
items.cn: 现代社会学用它指新来者变得像主流社会，语言学用它指相邻语音变得相似。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the connection of similis to simul is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin form is reconstructed, and the first date of each technical sense is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：similis 与 simul 的联系虽被一般接受，但其拉丁语之前形态属重构形式；各技术义的首见年代无法确定。

note.en: Group one shares the 'like' root; group two holds verbs of taking something in.
note.cn: 第一组共享「相似」词根；第二组是表示纳入某物的动词。

entries.definition: The process or result; the verb names the act that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或结果；动词指产生它的动作。

entries.definition: Describes someone or something already absorbed.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被吸收的人或物。

entries.definition: Describes the capacity to absorb or make similar.
entries.definitionCN: 描述吸收或同化的能力。

entries.definition: To make unlike or to become less similar; the prefix reverses the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同或变得不相似；前缀反转了方向。

entries.definition: The general verb for taking in liquid, heat or knowledge; it does not say the thing is remade.
entries.definitionCN: 指吸收液体、热量或知识的普通动词，不表示纳入之物被改造。

entries.definition: To bring parts into a working whole; it stresses structure more than likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 指把各部分带入一个运作整体，强调结构而非相似。

entries.definition: To break food or information down into usable form; assimilate stresses the later incorporation.
entries.definitionCN: 指把食物或信息分解为可用形式；assimilate 强调其后的并入。

entries.definition: To include something as part of a body or company; it is often organizational.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物作为身体或公司的一部分纳入，常用于组织语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real verb forms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实动词形式，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ad- 'toward' plus similis 'like': to move toward likeness.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 similis「相似」：朝相似移动。

normal.en: The verb family runs assimilate, assimilates, assimilated, assimilating, assimilation.
normal.cn: 动词词族包括 assimilate、assimilates、assimilated、assimilating、assimilation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: assimilate nutrients, assimilate information, assimilate into society.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：吸收营养、吸收信息、融入社会。

normal.en: The intransitive use describes people; the transitive use can describe food, facts or sounds.
normal.cn: 不及物用法描述人；及物用法可描述食物、事实或语音。

normal.en: Spelling note: the prefix ends in a voiced stop, but writing has merged it into the following hissing sound.
normal.cn: 注意双写的咝音：前缀末辅音在书写中已与后面的咝音合并。

abstract.en: Picture a cube of ice losing its edge in warm water.
abstract.cn: 想象一块冰在温水里失去棱角。

abstract.en: Picture a new song becoming hummable in a foreign key.
abstract.cn: 想象一首新歌在异国调子里变得随口可哼。

abstract.en: Picture a river carrying silt until the silt is simply part of the water.
abstract.cn: 想象河流携着泥沙，直到泥沙干脆成为水的一部分。

examples.en: It takes years to assimilate a second language well enough to joke in it.
examples.cn: 要把第二语言吸收到能开玩笑的程度，需要多年。

examples.en: The body cannot assimilate the mineral without enough fat in the diet.
examples.cn: 饮食中脂肪不足时，身体无法吸收这种矿物质。

examples.en: The new department was assimilated into the older one within a year.
examples.cn: 新部门在一年内被并入较老的部门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」加「相似」加「使……」——使外来的东西变得像自己

root: 拉丁 assimilare「使相似、吸收」= ad-（向）+ similis（相似），经法语进入英语。similis 一般认为与 simul「一起」同源，更早形态属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one intake: something outside is brought in and made to fit, whether it is food, information, a person, a sound, an office, an experience or a conquered people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次纳入展开：外部之物被带进来并被弄得合身，它可以是食物、信息、人、语音、机构、经历或被征服的民族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of ice dissolving in warm water until the whole glass carries its coolness.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块冰在温水中消融，直到整杯水都带着它的凉意。

branches.en: FOOD FIRST: the body turns foreign matter into tissue.
branches.cn: 食物在先：身体把外来物质变成组织。

branches.en: MIND: information and painful experience must be broken down before they become one's own.
branches.cn: 心智：信息与痛苦经历必须先被拆解，才能成为自己所有。

branches.en: PERSON AND GROUP: a newcomer becomes like the host without losing the ability to act.
branches.cn: 人与群体：新来者变得像主流，却不失行动能力。

branches.en: LIKENESS AND SOUND: one thing is made like another, down to a single phoneme.
branches.cn: 相似与语音：一物被弄得像另一物，小到一个音位。

branches.en: POWER: an office is merged, and a people can be swallowed by an empire.
branches.cn: 权力：机构被合并，民族也能被帝国吞并。

intro.en: Assimilate is a Latin verb of direction plus likeness, with a family of English nouns, adjectives and a reversed form.
intro.cn: assimilate 是一个由方向前缀与「相似」构成的拉丁动词，并有一族英语名词、形容词与一个反向形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis supplies similar and similarity; ad- turns the adjective into a verb of making, and dis- reverses it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 similis 衍生 similar 与 similarity；ad- 把这个形容词变成「使……」的动词，dis- 则反转方向。

items.example: The prefix aims the action at a target.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向目标。

items.example: The verb names the act of making one thing like another.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指使一物像另一物。

items.example: Assimilation can be cultural or physical.
items.exampleCN: 同化可以是文化的，也可以是生理的。

items.example: An assimilated group speaks the majority language.
items.exampleCN: 被同化的群体说多数人的语言。

derivatives.meaning: the process of becoming part of a whole

definition_zh: 同化；吸收；使某物融入更大的整体
definition_en: the process of becoming like something else, or of absorbing something into a larger whole
core_image: 一颗石子落进一锅浓汤，外形渐渐消失，味道却散进整锅汤里
scene: 新搬来的家庭在几年里改说当地语言、参加本地节庆，孩子们的同学不再觉得他们外来。Over two generations, the immigrant family achieved full assimilation into the host community.
sceneCN: 这里 assimilation 指「移民群体逐步融入主流社会的文化同化」（第 1 个义项：群体吸收进主流文化的过程）；句意为经过两代人，这个移民家庭完成了对当地社会的同化。可辨识物件：街区、节庆旗帜、学校门口、家庭餐桌。

pos.zh: 同化；融合（社会文化义，常作不可数）
吸收（生理、认知或语音义）

forms.label: 可数复数（具体过程或案例）

derivatives.zh: 异化（语音或文化上的反向过程）

senses.title: Cultural absorption into a host society
senses.titleCN: 融入主流社会的文化同化
senses.definition: the process by which a group or person takes on the culture of a host society
senses.definitionCN: 群体或个人逐渐接受主流社会文化的过程
senses.example: Over two generations, the immigrant family achieved full assimilation into the host community.
senses.exampleCN: 经过两代人，这个移民家庭完成了对当地社会的同化。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to make like'; in society the process makes newcomers like the majority.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使相似」；在社会层面，这个过程使新来者变得像多数人。

senses.title: Physiological absorption
senses.definition: the process by which the body takes nutrients into its own tissue
senses.definitionCN: 身体把营养纳入自身组织的过程
senses.example: Assimilation of nutrients begins in the small intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 营养的吸收从小肠开始。
senses.why: The body literally makes food like itself, turning foreign matter into tissue, which is the oldest concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 身体确实把食物变得像自己，把外来物质变成组织，这是最古老的具体义。

senses.title: Cognitive assimilation
senses.definition: the fitting of new experience into an existing mental framework
senses.definitionCN: 把新经验纳入既有心智框架
senses.example: Piaget described assimilation as fitting new experience into an existing schema.
senses.exampleCN: 皮亚杰把同化描述为把新经验纳入既有图式。
senses.why: The mind, like the body, absorbs what is new by making it fit what is already there.
senses.whyCN: 心智与身体一样，通过让新事物贴合已有之物来吸收它。

senses.title: Phonetic assimilation
senses.definition: the change of a speech sound so that it becomes more like a neighbouring sound
senses.definitionCN: 一个语音变得与相邻语音更相似
senses.example: In handbag the n of hand becomes m by assimilation before b.
senses.exampleCN: 在英语复合词「手袋」中，前一词尾的鼻音受后接双唇音影响，经同化变成双唇鼻音。
senses.why: Sounds, like people, adjust to their neighbours; the technical sense applies the old verb to pronunciation.
senses.whyCN: 音与人一样会向邻居靠拢；这个技术义把古老的动词用到发音上。

senses.title: Immigrant assimilation policy
senses.definition: a state programme that expects newcomers to adopt the majority culture
senses.definitionCN: 要求新来者接受多数文化的国家政策
senses.example: The city's assimilation policy offered language classes but demanded cultural surrender.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的同化政策提供语言课程，却要求文化上的归顺。
senses.why: When the process is planned by institutions, the noun names a policy and carries its political weight.
senses.whyCN: 当过程由机构规划时，这个名词指一项政策，并带上政治分量。

senses.title: Structural assimilation
senses.definition: entry of a minority into the institutions and social networks of the majority
senses.definitionCN: 少数群体进入多数群体的制度与社会网络
senses.example: Structural assimilation meant immigrants entered clubs, schools and political parties.
senses.exampleCN: 结构性同化意味着移民进入俱乐部、学校与政党。
senses.why: Sociologists split assimilation into parts; the structural part concerns access to institutions rather than taste or language.
senses.whyCN: 社会学家把同化分成若干部分；结构部分关乎制度准入，而非口味或语言。

senses.title: Forced assimilation
senses.definition: assimilation imposed by power, often through schools, law or punishment
senses.definitionCN: 由权力强加的同化，常通过学校、法律或惩罚
senses.example: Boarding schools practised forced assimilation of indigenous children.
senses.exampleCN: 寄宿学校对原住民儿童实行强制同化。
senses.why: The same noun can name coercion, because absorption into a larger whole may be demanded rather than chosen.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也能指强迫，因为融入更大整体可能是被要求而非自愿的。

senses.title: Abstract incorporation into a framework
senses.definition: the incorporation of a foreign element into an existing system or narrative
senses.definitionCN: 把外来要素并入既有体系或叙述
senses.example: The essay assimilates every dissent into one smooth narrative.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把一切异议都同化进一个平滑的叙述。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops people and bodies: any odd element can be made to fit a system.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义不再涉及人与身体：任何异质要素都可以被弄得贴合某个体系。

intro.en: Assimilation comes from Latin assimilatio, from assimilare 'to make like', built on ad- 'to' and similis 'like'. English uses it for bodies, minds, sounds and societies. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: assimilation 来自拉丁 assimilatio，源于 assimilare「使相似」，由 ad-「向」与 similis「相似」构成。英语用它指身体、心智、语音与社会。年代均为约数。

items.en: Similis meant 'like, similar'. It is generally connected with simul 'together' and similis 'like', but the pre-Latin shape is a reconstruction rather than a witnessed form.
items.cn: similis 意为「相似的」。一般认为它与 simul「一起」同源，但拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式，并无实际书证。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus similis produced assimilare 'to make like, to liken, to absorb'.
items.cn: ad-「向、朝」加 similis 构成 assimilare「使相似、比作、吸收」。

items.en: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century, first in the general sense of making one thing like another.
items.cn: 这个名词在十六世纪进入英语，最初泛指使一物像另一物。

items.en: Physiology adopted it for the conversion of food into tissue, and psychology later for the fitting of new experience into existing schemas.
items.cn: 生理学用它指食物转化为组织，心理学后来用它指把新经验纳入既有图式。

items.en: Nineteenth-century sociology applied it to immigrant groups, and linguistics used it for sounds becoming like their neighbours.
items.cn: 十九世纪社会学把它用于移民群体，语言学则用它指语音向邻近语音靠拢。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link of similis to simul is generally accepted but the pre-Latin form is reconstructed, and the earliest use of each technical sense is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：similis 与 simul 的联系虽被一般接受，但拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式；各技术义的最早书证年代并不精确。

note.en: Group one is built on the same 'like' root; group two names absorption or blending under other names.
note.cn: 第一组同出「相似」词根；第二组是用其他名称表达吸收或混合的说法。

entries.definition: The action behind the noun; it can take a direct object or appear in the passive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动作；可带宾语，也可用被动式。

entries.definition: Describes a person or group already absorbed, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被吸收的个人或群体，而非过程。

entries.definition: Means tending to absorb or make similar; it describes a capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 意为有吸收或同化倾向的；描述一种能力。

entries.definition: The reverse process, in which sounds or traits become less alike; the prefix changes the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 相反的过程，语音或特质变得更不相似；前缀改变了方向。

entries.definition: Entry into a society without necessarily losing one's own culture; assimilation is stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 进入社会但未必失去自身文化；同化的程度更强。

entries.definition: The plain word for one thing taking in another, used of liquids, knowledge and groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指一物吸纳另一物的普通说法，可用于液体、知识与群体。

entries.definition: Cultural change through contact that can go both ways; assimilation usually points toward the majority.
entries.definitionCN: 接触引起的文化变化，可是双向的；同化通常指向多数群体。

entries.definition: The result of many things becoming the same; it stresses sameness rather than absorption.
entries.definitionCN: 指许多事物变得相同的结果，强调相同而非吸收。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real contrasts, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实对比，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ad- 'toward' plus similis 'like': to move toward being like.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 similis「相似」：朝「像」的方向移动。

normal.en: The family runs assimilate, assimilated, assimilation, assimilative, assimilable, assimilationist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 assimilate、assimilated、assimilation、assimilative、assimilable、assimilationist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cultural assimilation, assimilation of immigrants, phonetic assimilation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：文化同化、移民的同化、语音同化。

normal.en: The same noun serves the stomach, the mind, the mouth and the state.
normal.cn: 同一个名词可用于胃、心智、口舌与国家。

normal.en: Opposite direction is marked by a different prefix in dissimilation.
normal.cn: 相反方向由 dissimilation 中的另一个前缀标记。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of sugar disappearing into hot tea.
abstract.cn: 想象一块糖消失在热茶里。

abstract.en: Picture a new word being spoken in the accent of its new street.
abstract.cn: 想象一个新词用它新所在街道的口音说出。

abstract.en: Picture a map redrawn until the old border is only a faint line.
abstract.cn: 想象地图被重画，旧边界只剩一道淡线。

examples.en: Assimilation into the village took a generation and cost the family its old language.
examples.cn: 融入这个村庄花了一代人的时间，也让这家人失去了旧语言。

examples.en: The laboratory measured the assimilation of iron in the digestive tract.
examples.cn: 实验室测量了消化道中铁的吸收。

examples.en: Linguists describe the assimilation of place of articulation in rapid speech.
examples.cn: 语言学家描述快速语流中发音部位的同化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」加「相似」加「过程」——朝「变得相似」走的过程

root: 拉丁 assimilare「使相似」= ad-（向）+ similis（相似），名词 assimilatio；similis 一般认为与 simul「一起」同源，但更早形态属重构。英语 assimilation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: something outside is made like the inside, whether the inside is a society, a body, a mind, a sound system or a written argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把外部之物变得像内部之物，这个「内部」可以是社会、身体、心智、语音系统或一篇论述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into thick soup, losing its outline while its taste spreads through the pot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子落进浓汤，外形渐失，味道却散进整锅。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND POLICY: a group may be absorbed by the majority, and the state may demand it.
branches.cn: 社会与政策：群体可能被多数吸收，国家也可能强制要求。

branches.en: BODY: food becomes tissue, the most concrete form of the process.
branches.cn: 身体：食物变成组织，这是该过程最具体的形式。

branches.en: MIND AND TEXT: new experience fits a schema, and an argument can absorb dissent.
branches.cn: 心智与文本：新经验贴合图式，一篇论述也能吸收异议。

branches.en: SOUND: a speech sound adjusts to its neighbour.
branches.cn: 语音：语音向邻近语音靠拢。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND FORCE: entry into schools and parties is different from compulsory absorption.
branches.cn: 制度与强制：进入学校与政党，不同于强迫吸收。

intro.en: Assimilation can be read from a Latin prefix, the Latin adjective for 'like', and the noun suffix that names a process.
intro.cn: assimilation 可以按拉丁前缀、表示「相似」的拉丁形容词，以及表示过程的名词后缀逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis supplies similar, similarity and assimilate; ad- adds direction toward, and the noun suffix names the process.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 similis 衍生 similar、similarity 与 assimilate；ad- 增添朝向，名词后缀指过程。

items.example: The prefix aims the action at a target.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向目标。

items.example: The adjective supplies the goal of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供动作的目标。

items.example: The verb names the act of making one thing like another.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指使一物像另一物。

items.meaning: the process of becoming like or being absorbed
items.example: Assimilation can be cultural or physical.
items.exampleCN: 同化可以是文化的，也可以是生理的。

items.example: An assimilated group speaks the majority language.
items.exampleCN: 被同化的群体说多数人的语言。

items.meaning: tending to absorb or make similar
items.example: The process is assimilative by nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程本质上是同化性的。

items.example: Some nutrients are more assimilable than others.
items.exampleCN: 有些营养比其他营养更易吸收。

items.example: The policy was defended by assimilationists.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策得到同化论者的辩护。

items.meaning: the reverse process, becoming less alike
items.exampleCN: 异化使相邻语音变得不同。

derivatives.meaning: to make unlike; to become less similar

definition_en: to help someone by doing part of the work, or to help make a goal
core_image: 有人站在旁边，伸手扶住摇晃的梯子
scene: 手术室里器械不断递到医生手边。A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 assist 是「协助」（第 1 个义项：在旁边帮忙）；句意是手术中一名护士协助外科医生。

senses.title: Help by sharing the work
senses.definition: to help someone, especially by doing part of their work
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人，尤其替他分担一部分工作
senses.example: A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术中一名护士协助外科医生。
senses.why: Assist comes from Latin assistere, 'to stand by', so the picture is someone standing beside you and lending a hand rather than taking over.
senses.whyCN: assist 源自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，画面是有人站到你身边搭把手，而不是代替你去做。

senses.title: Help make a goal
senses.definition: in sport, to pass or play so that another player scores
senses.definitionCN: 在体育比赛中传球配合，使队友得分
senses.example: He assisted the winning goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一分钟助攻了制胜球。
senses.why: The same image of standing beside and enabling another's success narrows in sport to the pass that lets a teammate score.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「站在旁边促成别人成功」的形象，在球场上收窄为那一脚让队友得分的传球。

intro.en: Assist is built from Latin words for standing, and its oldest picture is standing beside someone.
intro.cn: assist 由拉丁语中表示「站」的词构成，最古老的画面是站到某人身边。

items.en: sistere meant 'to stand, to place'.
items.cn: sistere 意为「站立、放置」。

items.en: assistere meant 'to take one's stand beside'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站到旁边」。

items.en: assister meant 'to be present and give help'.
items.cn: assister 意为「在场并给予帮助」。

items.en: English assisten meant 'to help or support'.
items.cn: 英语 assisten 意为「帮助、支援」。

items.en: Sport added the sense of setting up a goal.
items.cn: 体育领域增出「为进球做球」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sist root; the near-meaning group gives other verbs for helping.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sist 词根；近义组是其他表示帮助的动词。

abstract.en: See a nurse's hand arriving before it is asked for.
abstract.cn: 想象护士的手在开口之前就递到了。

abstract.en: See a pass rolled into the path of a runner.
abstract.cn: 想象一脚球滚到队友跑动的线路上。

examples.en: Two students assisted with the survey.

definition_en: help given to someone, especially official or financial help
core_image: 一只手从旁边伸过来，托住快要倒下的东西
scene: 老人提着两袋菜站在楼梯口。A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
sceneCN: 这里 assistance 是「帮助」（第 1 个义项：给予的援手）；句意是邻居主动帮忙提袋子。

senses.title: Help that is given
senses.definition: help that someone gives to another person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人给予另一个人的援手
senses.example: A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居主动帮忙提袋子。
senses.why: Assistance is assist plus -ance, a suffix naming a state or an act, so it treats the help as something handed over rather than as one person's deed.
senses.whyCN: assistance 是 assist 加 -ance，这个后缀表示状态或行为，因此它把帮助看作被递过来的一份援手，而不是某个人的一次动作。

senses.title: Official or financial aid
senses.definition: money or support provided by an institution or government
senses.definitionCN: 由机构或政府提供的钱款与支援
senses.example: The family applied for government assistance.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人申请了政府补助。
senses.why: When the hand that helps belongs to an office or a fund rather than a neighbour, the word settles into the sense of formal aid paid out by an institution.
senses.whyCN: 当伸出的手来自机构或基金而不是邻居时，这个词就固定指由机构发放的正式援助与补助。

intro.en: Assistance is the abstract noun of assist, made with a suffix of state and action.
intro.cn: assistance 是 assist 的抽象名词，由表示状态与行为的名词后缀构成。

definition_en: a person who helps someone more senior, or a junior rank
core_image: 站在主事者侧后方，随时接过手里的活
scene: 诊所里，年轻人先登记病人的信息。The assistant booked the next patient in.
sceneCN: 这里 assistant 是「助手」（第 1 个义项：协助他人工作的人）；句意是助手为下一位病人登记。

senses.title: Person who helps
senses.definition: a person employed to help someone with their work
senses.definitionCN: 受雇帮助某人完成工作的人
senses.example: The assistant booked the next patient in.
senses.exampleCN: 助手为下一位病人做了登记。
senses.why: The Latin ending -ant marks the doer, so assistant is literally 'the one standing beside', the person who takes part of the work off another's hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -ant 标记动作的执行者，所以 assistant 字面就是「站在旁边的那个人」，替别人分担一部分工作。

senses.title: Junior rank before a title

definition_en: A paid university post in which a graduate student teaches or helps with research, usually in return for a fee waiver and a stipend; also the tenure of that post.
core_image: 一边替教授带课，一边用这份工换掉学费单
scene: 她拿到一份带学费减免的助教职位。She was offered a teaching assistantship with a fee waiver.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：assistantship 指研究生担任助教或助研的有薪职位，常与学费减免绑在一起。

senses.title: A paid teaching or research post
senses.titleCN: 有薪的助教或助研职位
senses.definition: a university appointment for a graduate student who teaches classes or helps a research group for pay
senses.definitionCN: 给研究生的校内职位，通过带课或协助科研换取报酬
senses.example: The assistantship covers tuition and a monthly stipend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个助教职位覆盖学费并按月发放津贴。
senses.why: The ending -ship names an office, so the word means the position itself rather than the person holding it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 表示职位或身份，所以这个词指职位本身，而不是担任它的人。

senses.title: The tenure of that post

senses.definitionCN: 担任这一职位的期间或身份，如「在她任助教期间」
senses.example: During his assistantship he taught four sections.
senses.exampleCN: 任助教期间他带了四个班。
senses.why: English -ship freely turns a role into a stretch of time, exactly as it does in professorship and membership.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 -ship 能自如地把角色变成一段时间，professorship 与 membership 也是如此。

intro.en: Assistantship is assistant plus -ship: assist comes from Latin assistere, to stand by, from ad, to, plus sistere, to stand, and -ship is an Old English ending for an office.
intro.cn: assistantship 就是 assistant 加 -ship：assist 出自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，由 ad「向」加 sistere「站」构成；-ship 则是古英语表示职位的后缀。

items.en: Latin sistere meant to stand or to place, the base of a large family of standing words.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sistere 意为「站立、放置」，是一大批「站」类词的底座。

items.en: With ad, to, assistere meant to stand by someone, hence to help.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」后，assistere 意为「站在某人身旁」，因而引申为「帮助」。

items.en: Old French assister kept the sense of attending and helping, and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语 assister 保留「在旁协理」的意思，并传入英语。

items.en: English assistant named a person who stands by to help, with the agent ending -ant.
items.cn: 英语 assistant 用施事后缀 -ant 指「在旁帮忙的人」。

items.en: The ending -ship comes from Old English scipe, meaning shape, state or office, as in friendship.
items.cn: 后缀 -ship 源自古英语 scipe，意为「形态、状态、职位」，如 friendship。

items.en: American universities in the twentieth century made assistantship the standard term for funded graduate posts.
items.cn: 二十世纪美国大学把 assistantship 定为有资助研究生职位的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the assist family and adds two campus words with the same -ship ending; the near-meaning group lists other ways study is funded.
note.cn: 形近组保留 assist 词族，并加上两个同样以 -ship 结尾的校园词；近义组列出其他资助求学的方式。

normal.en: Countable: two assistantships, not much assistantship.

abstract.cn: 想象一张课表把学费单抵掉了。

abstract.en: Imagine a lab bench with your name on the rota.
abstract.cn: 想象实验台值班表上写着你的名字。

abstract.en: Think of a role you hold for two funded years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个由资助支撑两年的角色。

examples.cn: 她申请了物理系的助学职位。

examples.cn: 该系每年提供二十个助学职位。

examples.en: His assistantship was renewed for a third year.
examples.cn: 他的助教职位续到了第三年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：assist「协助」+ -ant「人」+ -ship「职位」——当助理的那个职位，就是 assistantship。

root: 拉丁语 sistere「站」加 ad-「向」构成 assistere「站在旁」，经古法语入英语 assist；加施事后缀 -ant 成 assistant，再加古英语 -scipe「职位」成 assistantship。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one office seen twice: the funded job itself, and the stretch of time you spend holding it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个职位被看了两遍：那份有资助的工作本身，以及担任它的那段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teaching timetable cancelling a tuition bill
core.cn: 核心意象：一边替教授带课，一边用这份工换掉学费单

An office and the time spent in it.
branches.cn: 一个职位，以及在其中的那段时间。

intro.en: Assistantship is as- from ad-, -sist from sistere, -ant for the doer and -ship for the office; the same layers build assistance and membership.

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is sistere, to stand, assistere, to stand by, and status, a standing position; -ship stays Germanic.

definition_zh: 联想；把……联系起来；交往；同事
definition_en: to connect things in the mind, to spend time with people, or a person you work with
core_image: 两条原本分开的线在脑中打了一个结
scene: 一闻到消毒水味，她就想起医院。That smell is associated with the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 associate 是「联想到」（第 1 个义项：把两件事在脑中连起来）；句意是那股气味让人联想到医院。

senses.title: Connect in the mind
senses.definition: to connect one thing with another in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中把一件事与另一件事连起来
senses.example: That smell is associated with the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味让人联想到医院。
senses.why: Associate comes from Latin associare, 'to join as a companion', built on socius 'companion', so the core act is pairing two things so that one calls up the other.
senses.whyCN: associate 源自拉丁语 associare「使结为同伴」，词基 socius 意为同伴，所以核心动作是把两样东西配成伴，见到一个就想起另一个。

senses.title: Spend time with people
senses.definition: to spend time with a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某群体经常相处
senses.example: He associates with artists and writers.
senses.exampleCN: 他常与画家和作家来往。
senses.why: When the companionship is between people rather than ideas, the same joining becomes the plain act of keeping company with a group.
senses.whyCN: 当「结伴」发生在人与人之间而不是概念之间时，同一个连接动作就落成了与某群人来往这一日常含义。

senses.title: Work partner
senses.definition: a person you work or do business with
senses.definitionCN: 一起工作或做生意的人
senses.example: She met a business associate at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她在机场见了一位生意伙伴。
senses.why: The noun form names the companion who has been joined to you by work, so it covers colleagues and business partners without implying friendship.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指因工作而与你结伴的人，因此既能指同事，也能指生意伙伴，并不暗示私人交情。

intro.en: Associate is built on the Latin word for a companion, and its senses all keep the idea of joining.
intro.cn: associate 建立在拉丁语「同伴」一词上，各义项都保留「结成伴」的意思。

items.en: socius meant 'companion or ally'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」。

items.en: associare meant 'to join with as a companion'.
items.cn: associare 意为「结为同伴」。

items.en: associer meant 'to unite or combine'.
items.cn: associer 意为「联合、结合」。

items.en: English associate covered both company and mental linking.
items.cn: 英语 associate 兼指结伴与脑中的联系。

items.en: The noun sense 'colleague' settled in business use.
items.cn: 名词「同事」义在商业语境中固定下来。

note.cn: 形近组共享 soci 词根；近义组是表示连接与交往的动词。

definition_en: an organized group, or a connection between things
core_image: 一群人围着同一张桌子坐下
scene: 街角的老楼门口挂起一块新牌子。The residents formed an association to save the building.
sceneCN: 这里 association 是「协会」（第 1 个义项：为共同目的组成的团体）；句意是居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。

senses.title: Organized group
senses.definition: an organized group of people with a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目的组织起来的一群人
senses.example: The residents formed an association to save the building.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。
senses.why: Association is associate plus -ion, so a verb meaning 'to join as companions' becomes the body of companions who have joined, that is, an organized group.
senses.whyCN: association 是 associate 加 -ion，把「结为同伴」的动词变成结成伴的那一群人，也就是有组织的团体。

senses.title: Connection or mental link
senses.definition: a connection between two things, including one made in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的关联，也包括脑中的联想
senses.example: The study found an association between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现了睡眠与记忆之间的关联。
senses.why: The same joining, once it is between facts or ideas rather than people, becomes a link that can be measured or merely felt in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「结伴」如果发生在事实或观念之间而不是人之间，就成了可以被测量或只在脑中感到的关联。

intro.en: Association is the noun of joining, used both for groups of people and for links between things.
intro.cn: association 是表示「结合」的名词，既指人的团体，也指事物之间的关联。

items.en: Association named a guild or a body of people.

definition_en: to suppose without proof, to take on a duty, or to begin to have a quality
core_image: 一件外套被人直接披到自己身上
scene: 会议没核对数据就开始讨论。Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
sceneCN: 这里 assume 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：没有证据就先当作成立）；句意是大家都假定这些数字是对的。

senses.title: Suppose without proof
senses.definition: to believe that something is true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 在没有证据时先认定某事成立
senses.example: Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。
senses.why: Assume comes from Latin assumere, 'to take up', so taking a claim up as your own is to accept it before it has been proved.
senses.whyCN: assume 源自拉丁语 assumere「拿起来」，把一种说法拿过来当作自己的，就是在被证实之前先接受它。

senses.title: Take on a duty
senses.definition: to take on responsibility, power or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过责任、权力或职位
senses.example: She assumed control of the company in June.
senses.exampleCN: 她在六月接管了公司。
senses.why: The literal Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives here: power or duty is picked up and carried by the new holder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的本义在这个义项里保留下来：权力或责任被新的承担者接过去扛起来。

senses.title: Begin to have a quality
senses.definition: to begin to have a particular quality or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 开始带有某种性质或外表
senses.example: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。
senses.why: Putting on an appearance is the same gesture as putting on a coat, so the word can describe a look that something takes on.
senses.whyCN: 把某种外表披到自己身上，与披上一件外套是同一个动作，因此这个词也能说某物呈现出某种样子。

intro.en: Assume is a Latin verb of taking, and every sense keeps something of that gesture.
intro.cn: assume 是拉丁语中表示「拿取」的动词，各个义项都保留着这个动作的影子。

normalIntro.cn: assume 始终是一个「拿」的动作：拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表。

normal.en: The pattern assume that is common in argument.
normal.cn: 论证中常见 assume that 结构。

normal.en: Assume responsibility is the formal way to say take the blame or duty.
normal.cn: assume responsibility 是承担责任的正式说法。

normal.en: The past participle assumed can mean pretended.

normal.en: Do not confuse assume with presume, which is based on likelihood.

normal.en: The s sounds like a soft z in the middle.

abstract.en: See a coat lifted from a hook and put on without asking.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套被从钩子上取下，不问自穿。

abstract.en: See a signature on a line that says responsibility.
abstract.cn: 想象在写着「责任」的那一栏签下名字。

abstract.en: See a face turning the colour of the sky before rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸变成雨前天空的颜色。

examples.cn: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。

examples.en: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。

sensesIntro.cn: 拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表，是同一个「取」的动作面对三种对象。

intro.cn: 词根 sume 意为「拿」，贯穿 consume、resume 与 presume。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sumere 是词基，它的复合词遍布日常英语。

definition_en: something accepted as true without proof, or the act of taking on a duty
core_image: 一块没有验过的地基被当作稳固
scene: 报告开头先列了三条前提。The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
sceneCN: 这里 assumption 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：未经验证就被接受的前提）；句意是计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。

senses.title: Thing taken as true
senses.definition: something you accept as true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 未经证明就被当作成立的前提
senses.example: The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。
senses.why: Assumption is assume plus -tion, turning the act of taking a claim up into the claim itself, the thing a plan leans on before proof arrives.
senses.whyCN: assumption 是 assume 加 -tion，把「拿过来接受」的动作变成被接受的那条内容，也就是计划在证据到来前所倚靠的前提。

senses.title: Act of taking on
senses.definition: the act of taking on power, duty or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过权力、职责或职位的行为
senses.example: The assumption of office takes place in May.
senses.exampleCN: 就职仪式在五月举行。
senses.why: The old Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives as a formal noun for entering an office or taking up a duty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的旧义保留下来，成为正式说法，指就任职位或承担职责。

intro.en: Assumption is the noun of taking up, whether a belief or an office.
intro.cn: assumption 是「拿起、接过」的名词，接过的可以是一种看法，也可以是一个职位。

normalIntro.en: An assumption is a floor nobody has tested before building on it.
normalIntro.cn: assumption 是一块没验过就被踩上去的地板。

normal.en: The phrase on the assumption that introduces the unproved point.
normal.cn: 短语 on the assumption that 引出那个未经验证的判断。

normal.en: In academic writing assumptions are usually stated and then tested.
normal.cn: 学术写作里通常先点明假设，再加以检验。

normal.en: The second sense is formal and appears with office or power.
normal.cn: 第二个义项较正式，常与职位或权力连用。

normal.en: The ending is -tion, so the noun refers to a thing or an act.
normal.cn: 结尾是 -tion，因此名词指事物或行为。

normal.en: Do not write an assumption of that for the everyday sense.
normal.cn: 日常「假定」义不用 an assumption of that 这种结构。

abstract.en: See a house built on a slab nobody checked.
abstract.cn: 想象房子盖在一块没人检查过的板上。

abstract.en: See a question mark drawn over a number in a report.
abstract.cn: 想象报告里的数字上被画了问号。

abstract.en: See a hand receiving a seal of office.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手接过任职印章。

examples.en: The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
examples.cn: 计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。

examples.en: The assumption of office takes place in May.

sensesIntro.en: A belief picked up without proof and an office picked up in ceremony are both things taken.
sensesIntro.cn: 未经证明就接受的看法，与在仪式上接过的职位，都是被「拿起」的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a floor laid down before anyone tests it.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人验过就铺好的地板。

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin sense of taking, with -tion marking the result.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留拉丁语「拿取」之义，-tion 标记结果。

latinIntro.cn: sumere「拿」产生了一整组以 -tion 结尾的英语名词。

definition_zh: 保证；把握；自信；安心；保险；质量保证；厚颜
definition_en: a making sure, whether by a promise that removes doubt, a state of certainty, a policy against loss, or too much confidence in oneself
core_image: 一个人把手按在另一个人的肩上，说一声“放心”——把对方心里的不安换成确定
scene: 餐桌上父亲郑重向女儿许诺，办公室里职员递出保单，年轻人走进面试间，仿佛那份工作已属于他。一个词，涵盖三种笃定。The father's promise to his daughter is an assurance that he will be there.
sceneCN: 这里 assurance 是「保证」（第 1 个义项：旨在使某人安心的郑重承诺）；句意：厨房桌边，父亲向女儿保证他一定会到，这句承诺就是一个保证。场景要点：厨房桌、父亲与女儿、寿险文件、面试门口。

senses.title: A word given to remove doubt
senses.titleCN: 保证：一句话把疑虑拿掉
senses.definition: a formal or solemn promise meant to give someone confidence
senses.definitionCN: 旨在使某人安心的正式或郑重承诺
senses.example: The company gave an assurance that no jobs would be cut.
senses.exampleCN: 公司保证不会裁员。
senses.why: Late 14c., 'formal or solemn pledge, promise', from Old French asseurance. The noun of -ance names the act of making sure, and a promise is the cheapest instrument for making another mind sure.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪末的“正式或郑重承诺”来自古法语 asseurance。这个 -ance 名词命名“使确定”的动作，而承诺是使另一颗心确定起来最便宜的工具。

senses.title: Certainty in the mind
senses.titleCN: 把握：心里再无怀疑的那种确定
senses.definition: full confidence or certainty that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 对某事为真或将会发生的充分信心或确定
senses.example: She spoke with the assurance of someone who had checked every figure.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话时带着一种查过每个数字的人才有的把握。
senses.why: The same late 14c. entry also meant 'certainty, full confidence'. The noun names both the act of making sure and the state of being sure, because -ance can take either side of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 14 世纪末的词条还兼指“确定、充分信心”。这个名词既命名“使确定”的动作，也命名“已确定”的状态，因为 -ance 可以取动词的两面。

senses.title: Carrying yourself as if you cannot fail
senses.titleCN: 自信：走起路来像不会失败
senses.definition: self-confidence, especially in manner or bearing
senses.definitionCN: 自信，尤指态度或举止上的
senses.example: Years of stage work gave her a quiet assurance.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的舞台经历给了她一种安静的自信。
senses.why: The sense 'self-confident' is recorded from the 1590s. Making others sure of you turns inward: the same act now has one's own self as its object.
senses.whyCN: “自信”义记录于 16 世纪 90 年代。使别人对你确定，转向了内部：同一个动作，如今对象成了自己。

senses.title: The calm that follows being told
senses.titleCN: 安心：被告知之后的那口气
senses.definition: a feeling of relief and freedom from worry produced by a promise or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 因承诺或解释而获得的宽慰、免于忧虑之感
senses.example: His assurance that the train would wait let her breathe again.
senses.exampleCN: 他保证火车会等，这才让她重新喘上气来。
senses.why: The verb assure meant 'reassure, give confidence to' from late 14c. Latin securus is literally 'free from care' (se- 'without' + cura 'care'), so assurance names the removal of care rather than the promise that removes it.
senses.whyCN: 动词 assure 从 14 世纪末就意为“使安心、给信心”。拉丁语 securus 字面是“无忧”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”），所以 assurance 命名的是忧虑被拿掉，而不是拿掉它的那句承诺。

senses.title: A policy against loss
senses.titleCN: 保险：用一笔钱买下“不会损失”
senses.definition: insurance, especially life insurance (British usage)
senses.definitionCN: 保险，尤指人寿保险（英式用法）
senses.example: He took out a life assurance policy when his first child was born.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个孩子出生时，他买了一份人寿保险。
senses.why: Assurance was the older English word for commercial insurance from the late 16c.; insurance, its en- variant, took over in the 1650s. A premium buys a written promise that loss will be made sure against.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪末起，assurance 就是商业保险较早的英语说法；它的 en- 变体 insurance 在 17 世纪 50 年代接手。保费买下的是一纸承诺：损失会被“确保”抵挡。

senses.title: Quality made certain by process
senses.titleCN: 质量保证：靠流程把质量做成确定
senses.definition: the part of a business that systematically checks that products meet a standard
senses.definitionCN: 企业系统检查产品是否符合标准的部分
senses.example: Quality assurance caught the fault before the parts left the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 质量保证在零件出厂前就查出了缺陷。
senses.why: Twentieth-century industry moved assurance from a spoken promise to a procedure: instead of assuring a customer in words, a firm builds certainty into every step. The abstract noun becomes the name of a department.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的工业把 assurance 从口头承诺变成流程：企业不再用话向客户保证，而是把确定性做进每一道工序。抽象名词于是成了一个部门的名称。

senses.title: A guarantee that something holds
senses.titleCN: 保障：保证某件事站得住
senses.definition: a guarantee that something exists, continues, or is adequate
senses.definitionCN: 对某物存在、持续或足够充分的保证
senses.example: The treaty offers an assurance of water supply to the lower valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约为下游河谷提供了供水保障。
senses.why: Here assurance is followed by of rather than that: the noun names the thing made certain, not the sentence spoken. It is the same 'making sure', shifted from a hearer's mind to a fact in the world.
senses.whyCN: 这里 assurance 后接 of 而不是 that：名词命名的是被确保的那件事，而不是说出的那句话。还是同一个“使确定”，只是从听者的心里移到了世上的一个事实。

senses.title: Too much sureness of oneself
senses.definition: impudence or presumption in manner (18th-century shading, now rare)
senses.definitionCN: 举止上的放肆、冒昧（18 世纪色彩，今罕用）
senses.example: He had the assurance to ask for a raise in his first week.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟有脸在上班第一周就要求加薪。
senses.why: The word had a negative tinge in the 18c., often suggesting impudence or presumption. There is a point where being sure of oneself stops looking like calm and starts looking like a claim on others.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 18 世纪带有贬义色彩，常指放肆或冒昧。对自己有把握，到某一点就不再像从容，而像对别人提要求。

senses.title: The deed that makes a right sure
senses.titleCN: 担保契据：让权利站得住的那张纸
senses.definition: a formal deed or clause that makes a right, title, or payment certain (legal)
senses.definitionCN: 使权利、所有权或付款成为确定的正式契据或条款（法律）
senses.example: The solicitor prepared an assurance of the title for the buyer.
senses.exampleCN: 律师为买方准备了一份产权担保契据。
senses.why: English -ance nouns often name the instrument as well as the act. In conveyancing an assurance is the deed that makes a title sure, just as a promise makes a mind sure.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 -ance 名词常同时命名动作和凭据。在不动产转让中，assurance 就是让产权站得住的那张契据，正如承诺让一颗心站得住。

intro.en: Assurance is assure plus -ance. Assure came through Old French asseurer from Vulgar Latin *assecurar, ad- 'to' plus securus 'free from care'; -ance makes an abstract noun of the act or state. The shift runs from 'making someone care-free' to 'a pledge', to 'certainty', to 'self-confidence', and finally to 'insurance'.
intro.cn: assurance 是 assure 加 -ance。assure 经古法语 asseurer 来自俗拉丁语 *assecurar，即 ad-“向”加 securus“无忧”；-ance 把动作或状态变成抽象名词。语义从“使某人无忧”走到“承诺”，再到“确定”“自信”，最后到“保险”。

items.en: Securus meant 'free from care, safe, secure', built from se- 'without, apart' plus cura 'care, anxiety'. The adjective describes a person, not a lock: to be secure is to have no care in the mind.
items.cn: securus 意为“无忧的、安全的、稳固的”，由 se-“无、离开”加 cura“忧虑、照料”构成。这个形容词描述的是人，不是锁：secure 就是心里没有忧虑。

items.en: The verb *assecurar, ad- plus securus, meant 'to make free from care'. The starred form is a reconstruction with no written record, so its exact shape is marked source uncertain; only its descendants in French and English are attested.
items.cn: 动词 *assecurar 由 ad- 加 securus 构成，意为“使无忧”。带星号的形式是没有书面记录的重构，因此其确切形态标为“来源不确定”；只有它在法语和英语中的后裔有文献可证。

items.en: Asseurer meant 'to reassure, calm, protect, to render sure', and the noun asseurance (11c.) meant 'assurance, promise; truce; certainty, safety, security'. Old French had already spread the word across trust, calm, and safety.
items.cn: asseurer 意为“使安心、使平静、保护、使确定”，名词 asseurance（11 世纪）意为“保证、承诺；停战；确定、安全、稳固”。古法语已经把这个词铺展到信任、平静与安全三个方面。

items.en: Assurance enters English as both 'formal or solemn pledge, promise' and 'certainty, full confidence'. Assure follows in the same period, meaning 'reassure, give confidence to; make secure; bind by a pledge'.
items.cn: assurance 进入英语时兼有“正式或郑重承诺”与“确定、充分信心”两义。assure 也在同一时期出现，意为“使安心、给信心；使安全；以承诺约束”。

items.en: 'Self-confident' is recorded from the 1590s. In the 18c. the word took a negative tinge, often suggesting impudence or presumption: too much assurance became a social fault.
items.cn: “自信”义记录于 16 世纪 90 年代。到 18 世纪，这个词带上贬义色彩，常指放肆或冒昧：过多的 assurance 成了一种社交过失。

items.en: Assurance was the older term for commercial insurance from the late 16c.; insurance, its en- variant, became standard in the 1650s. In the 20c. quality assurance turned the promise into a procedure, and the word acquired its modern office meaning.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪末起，assurance 是商业保险的较早说法；它的 en- 变体 insurance 在 17 世纪 50 年代成为标准。20 世纪，quality assurance 把承诺变成流程，这个词又添了现代的企业部门义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on sure/secur-: insurance and reassure are true relatives with different prefixes. Endurance merely rhymes in shape and comes from durus 'hard', so it must be kept apart.
note.cn: 形近组建立在 sure/secur- 上：insurance 与 reassure 都是换前缀的真同族。endurance 只是外形相押，来自 durus“坚硬”，必须分开。

entries.definition: cover against loss in exchange for payment. It is the en- twin of assurance and now the standard commercial term.
entries.definitionCN: 以付费换取损失保障。它是 assurance 的 en- 双胞胎，如今是标准的商业术语。

entries.definition: to make someone sure or free from doubt. Assurance is the state or act that the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人确定、使免于疑虑。assurance 是这动词所产生的状态或行为。

entries.definition: comfort given to remove fear a second time. It repeats the making-sure with re-.
entries.definitionCN: 再次消除恐惧的安慰。它用 re- 重复了“使确定”这个动作。

entries.definition: the power to bear hardship, from durus 'hard'. The -ance ending is shared, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 忍耐力，来自 durus“坚硬”。词尾 -ance 相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: a promise that something will be done or will work. It is the most enforceable synonym of assurance.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事将做到或能奏效的承诺。它是 assurance 最具可执行性的同义词。

entries.definition: a serious promise, often with something given as security. It matches the formal tone of assurance.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重的承诺，常以某物作担保。它对应 assurance 的正式语气。

entries.definition: the quality of being definitely true or known. It is assurance as a state of mind or fact.
entries.definitionCN: 确定无疑的性质。它是作为心理或事实状态的 assurance。

entries.definition: belief in one's own or another's ability. It overlaps assurance in both the self and the promise senses.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己或他人能力的信任。它在“自信”和“可托付”两层上都与 assurance 重叠。

entries.definition: a written promise that goods will be repaired or replaced. It is assurance limited to a product.
entries.definitionCN: 对商品将维修或更换的书面承诺。它是被限定在商品上的 assurance。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: ad- 'to', securus 'free from care', -ance 'state of'. Assurance is literally the act of putting someone beyond care.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：ad-“向”、securus“无忧”、-ance“状态”。assurance 字面上就是把某人放到忧虑之外。

normal.en: assurance = as- (ad-, 'to') + sure ('certain') + -ance: making someone certain.
normal.cn: assurance = as-（ad-，“向”）+ sure（“确定”）+ -ance：使某人确定。

normal.en: The sure family runs through assure, reassure, ensure, insure, and secure.
normal.cn: sure 词族贯穿 assure、reassure、ensure、insure、secure。

normal.en: Insurance is the en- twin of assurance: same promise, different prefix.
normal.cn: insurance 是 assurance 的 en- 双胞胎：同一个承诺，不同的前缀。

normal.en: Quality assurance is a promise turned into a checklist.
normal.cn: quality assurance 是被做成了检查表的承诺。

normal.en: To speak with assurance is to sound as if your words had already been checked.
normal.cn: speak with assurance，就是听起来像你的话已经被核对过了。

abstract.en: Sureness is pictured as a weight lifted off the chest: securus is literally 'without care'.
abstract.cn: “确定”被画成从胸口搬走的一块重物：securus 字面就是“没有忧虑”。

abstract.en: The word travels from the hearer's mind to the speaker's manner: first you calm him, then you look calm yourself.
abstract.cn: 这个词从听者的心里走到说者的姿态：先让他安定，再让自己看起来安定。

abstract.en: A promise, a policy, and a deed are three ways of writing the same sentence: this will not fail you.
abstract.cn: 一句承诺、一份保单、一张契据，是同一句话的三种写法：它不会辜负你。

examples.en: The minister refused to give any assurance about the timing of the vote.
examples.cn: 部长拒绝就投票时间作出任何保证。

examples.en: She answered the hostile questions with the assurance of a practised speaker.
examples.cn: 她以老练演讲者的自信回答了那些敌意提问。

examples.en: In Britain, life assurance is often sold alongside a mortgage.
examples.cn: 在英国，人寿保险常与按揭一起销售。

dict_mnemonic.text: as（去）+ sure（确定）+ ance（名词）——去把“确定”给他，就是保证；谐音“额秀润斯”：额（我）秀（sure）润（ance）——拍胸脯让他放心 → assurance 保证；自信

root: 源自拉丁语 securus“无忧的”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”），经俗拉丁语 *assecurar、古法语 asseurer 进入英语；-ance 为抽象名词后缀，核心是“使某人心里无忧、确定”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one removal of care. A promise takes doubt out of another mind; certainty and self-confidence keep it out of one's own; insurance and quality assurance sell the removal; and too much of it turns into impudence.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一次“拿走忧虑”。承诺把疑虑从别人心里拿走；确定与自信把它从自己心里拿走；保险与质量保证把这次“拿走”拿来出售；而拿走得太多，就变成了厚颜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: making someone care-free — a hand on the shoulder, a word given, a policy signed.
core.cn: 核心意象：使某人无忧——一只手按在肩上，一句话给出，一份保单签下。

branches.en: THE PROMISE AND THE CALM: the word given, and the relief it leaves in the hearer.
branches.cn: 承诺与安心：给出的那句话，以及它在听者心里留下的宽慰。

branches.en: CERTAINTY AND SAFEGUARD: a fact held sure in the mind, and a fact made sure in the world.
branches.cn: 确定与保障：在心里被拿稳的事实，以及在世上被确保的事实。

branches.en: SELF-ASSURANCE: the calm of the capable, sliding into the impudence of the over-sure.
branches.cn: 自信：能者的从容，滑向过度自信者的放肆。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL FORMS: a policy sold against loss, a procedure built to prevent it.
branches.cn: 制度化形态：为抵御损失而卖的保单，为预防损失而建的流程。

branches.en: THE DEED: the same making-sure written down and sealed.
branches.cn: 契据：同一个“使确定”被写下来并盖了章。

intro.en: Assurance is assure plus -ance. Assure is ad- plus the sure/secur- base, so the word is prefix, root, and abstract ending in that order. The ending lets the same noun mean the act of assuring and the state of being assured.
intro.cn: assurance 是 assure 加 -ance。assure 是 ad- 加 sure/secur- 词根，所以整词依次是前缀、词根、抽象后缀。后缀让同一个名词既能指“使确定”的动作，也能指“已确定”的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin securus 'free from care' (se- 'without' + cura 'care') is the root of sure, secure, security, assure, assurance, insure and insurance. The prefixes ad-, re-, in-, en- each redirect the same 'care-free' idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus“无忧”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”）是 sure、secure、security、assure、assurance、insure、insurance 的词根。前缀 ad-、re-、in-、en- 各自把同一个“无忧”观念转向不同方向。

items.meaning: to make someone free from doubt
items.example: He assured her that the door had been locked.
items.exampleCN: 他向她保证门已经锁好了。

items.example: She needed an assurance before she signed.
items.exampleCN: 签字之前她需要一个保证。

items.example: Are you sure the key is in your bag?
items.exampleCN: 你确定钥匙在你包里吗？

items.example: The documents are secure in the vault.
items.exampleCN: 文件在保险库里很安全。

items.meaning: to make certain against loss by paying
items.example: They insured the painting for two million.
items.exampleCN: 他们为这幅画投保了两百万。
这份保单包含旅行保险。

items.meaning: to make something certain to happen
items.example: Please ensure that the window is closed.
An assured income let him write full time.
items.exampleCN: 一份有保障的收入让他能全职写作。

definition_en: to tell someone confidently that something is true, or to make it certain
core_image: 一只手按住对方的手背，说一句放心
scene: 登机前机长在广播里说明情况。The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
sceneCN: 这里 assure 是「向……保证」（第 1 个义项：让对方确信某事）；句意是机长向我们保证航班安全。

pos.zh: 动词：向……保证；使确信；确保

derivatives.zh: 形容词：确信的；有把握的

senses.title: Make someone certain
senses.definition: to tell someone confidently that something is true so they stop worrying
senses.definitionCN: 肯定地告诉对方某事为真，使其不再担心
senses.example: The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
senses.exampleCN: 机长向我们保证航班是安全的。
senses.why: Assure comes from Latin assecurare, 'to make secure', built on securus 'free from care', so the core act is removing someone's worry rather than merely stating a fact.
senses.whyCN: assure 源自拉丁语 assecurare「使安全」，词基 securus 意为「无忧」，所以它的核心是替对方消除担心，而不只是陈述事实。

senses.title: Make certain to happen
senses.definition: to make something certain to happen or be obtained
senses.definitionCN: 使某事确定发生或确定得到
senses.example: Hard work assured his place in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 努力让他在队里站稳了位置。
senses.why: When the calming is done by events rather than words, the same 'make secure' means making an outcome certain.
senses.whyCN: 当让人安心的不是言语而是事情本身时，同一个「使稳固」就变成让某个结果确定无疑。

intro.en: Assure began as a word about making people free from care.
intro.cn: assure 起初是个让人免于忧虑的词。

items.en: securus meant 'free from care'.
items.cn: securus 意为「无忧的」。

items.en: assecurare meant 'to make secure'.
items.cn: assecurare 意为「使安稳」。

items.en: asseurer meant 'to promise and calm'.
items.cn: asseurer 意为「保证并安抚」。

items.en: English assure covered both promising and securing.
items.cn: 英语 assure 兼指保证与确保。

items.en: The word settled in formal promises and insurance.
items.cn: 这个词固定在正式承诺与保险语境中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sure family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of promising.
note.cn: 形近组是 sure 词族；近义组是表示承诺的动词。

to make certain

to promise formally
to say one will do something

normalIntro.en: To assure is to hand someone a reason to stop worrying.
normalIntro.cn: assure 就是递给对方一个不必担心的理由。

normal.en: The object is a person: assure the passengers.
normal.cn: 宾语是人：向乘客保证。

normal.en: Use assure someone of something or assure someone that.
normal.cn: 用 assure someone of something 或 assure someone that。

normal.en: Rest assured is a fixed phrase meaning be sure.
normal.cn: rest assured 是固定说法，意为请放心。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with ensure, which means make certain.
normal.cn: 不要与 ensure 混淆，后者意为确保。

normal.en: The ending sounds like sure.
normal.cn: 词尾读音与 sure 相同。

abstract.en: See a hand pressed briefly over another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在另一只手背上轻按一下。

abstract.en: See a seat belt sign switched off after the words are spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象广播说完后安全带指示灯熄灭。

abstract.en: See a knot pulled tight so it cannot slip.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被拉紧，不会松开。

examples.en: The captain assured us that the flight was safe.
examples.cn: 机长向我们保证航班是安全的。

examples.en: Hard work assured his place in the team.
examples.cn: 努力让他在队里站稳了位置。

examples.en: She assured me of her support.
examples.cn: 她向我保证会支持我。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 sure（安稳）：把安稳送到对方心里，就是让对方确信；把事情办到没有疑问，就是确保。

root: 源自拉丁语 assecurare「使安稳」，词基 securus 意为「无忧」，经古法语 asseurer 进入英语；由「让人安心」引申为口头保证，再由「使确定」引申为确保。

sensesIntro.en: Words can calm a person, and facts can settle an outcome; both remove doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 言语能安抚人，事实能定下结果，两者都在消除疑问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed down to steady another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按下去，让另一只手稳住。

branches.en: assure a place in the team
