intro.cn: 词根 sure 意为「无忧」，把 assure 与 ensure、insure 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin securus, 'free from care', also gives secure and security.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus「无忧」也是 secure 与 security 的来源。

definition_zh: n. 小行星（绕日运行的岩质小天体）；海星（旧动物学用法）
definition_en: A small rocky body orbiting the sun, most of them between Mars and Jupiter; in older zoological use, a starfish.
core_image: 望远镜里一个像星点却会移动的小石头
scene: 望远镜记录到一颗掠过地球轨道的岩质小天体。The telescope tracked a rocky asteroid past our orbit.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：asteroid 指绕太阳运行的小行星，比行星小得多。

senses.title: A small rocky body in orbit
senses.titleCN: 绕日运行的岩质小天体
senses.definition: a rocky object circling the sun, far smaller than a planet, most lying between Mars and Jupiter
senses.definitionCN: 绕太阳运行的岩质天体，远小于行星，多数位于火星与木星之间
senses.example: The probe landed on an asteroid after a long chase.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器长途追赶后降落在一颗小行星上。
senses.why: The name means star-like: through early telescopes these bodies looked like stars but moved against them.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字意为「像星的」：在早期望远镜里，这些天体看着像恒星，却相对恒星在移动。

senses.title: A starfish in older usage
senses.definition: in older zoological writing, a member of the starfish group, named for the same star shape
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的动物学文献中指海星类动物，命名同样取自星形
senses.example: The old plate labels the specimen an asteroid.
senses.exampleCN: 那张旧图版把这件标本标为海星。
senses.why: The same star-like ending serves both sky and sea, because the shape, not the material, gave the name.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「像星」的后缀既用于天空也用于海洋，因为命名依据是形状而不是材质。

intro.en: Asteroid is Greek asteroeides, star-like, from aster, star, plus eidos, form; Herschel proposed it in 1802 for the new bodies Ceres and Pallas.
intro.cn: asteroid 就是希腊语 asteroeides「像星的」，由 aster「星」加 eidos「形状」构成；1802 年赫歇尔为新发现的谷神星与智神星提出这个名字。

items.en: A reconstructed root for star lies behind Greek aster, Latin stella and English star alike.
items.cn: 一个表示「星」的拟构词根同时藏在希腊语 aster、拉丁语 stella 与英语 star 背后。

items.en: Greek aster meant star, and also any star-shaped figure, which is why flowers and cells took the name.
items.cn: 希腊语 aster 意为「星」，也指任何星形图案，所以花与细胞也借用了这个名字。

items.en: Greek eidos meant form or shape, and gives the ending -oid, meaning resembling.
items.cn: 希腊语 eidos 意为「形状」，产生后缀 -oid，意为「像……的」。

items.en: The compound asteroeides meant star-like, a description rather than a name.
items.cn: 复合词 asteroeides 意为「像星的」，本是描述而非名称。

items.en: Herschel proposed asteroid because the new bodies showed a star-like point instead of a planetary disc.
items.cn: 赫歇尔提出 asteroid，因为这些新天体呈星点状，而不是行星那样的圆面。

items.en: As hundreds were found between Mars and Jupiter, the word came to name a whole population of small bodies.
items.cn: 随着火星与木星之间发现数以百计的此类天体，这个词转而指一整群小天体。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the star root and shows two medical words with the same -oid ending; the near-meaning group sorts small bodies by size and stuff.
note.cn: 形近组保留「星」词根，并展示两个同样以 -oid 结尾的医学词；近义组按大小与成分区分小天体。

entries.definition: A star-shaped figure in a dividing cell.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞分裂时的星状结构。

entries.definition: Relating to the stars.
A gland in the neck that sets body pace.
entries.definitionCN: 颈部调节身体节奏的腺体。

entries.definition: A swollen vein near the lower bowel.
entries.definitionCN: 肠道末端附近肿胀的血管。

entries.definition: A small rock travelling through space.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间中穿行的小岩块。

entries.definition: An icy body that grows a tail near the sun.
entries.definitionCN: 接近太阳时生出一条尾的冰质天体。

entries.definition: An older word for a small planet-like body.
The formal term for such an orbiting body.
entries.definitionCN: 此类绕日天体的正式称法。

normalIntro.en: Asteroid is aster, star, plus -oid, resembling: a point of light that looks like a star but moves.
normalIntro.cn: asteroid 就是 aster「星」加 -oid「像……的」：一个看着像星、却会移动的光点。

normal.en: The ending -oid always means resembling.
normal.cn: 后缀 -oid 一律表示「像……的」。

normal.en: Aster, astral and astronomy share the root.
normal.cn: aster、astral、astronomy 共用这个词根。

normal.en: Most asteroids sit between Mars and Jupiter.
normal.cn: 多数小行星位于火星与木星之间。

normal.en: A meteoroid is smaller, a comet is icy.
normal.cn: meteoroid 更小，comet 含冰。

normal.en: The same word once meant starfish.
normal.cn: 同一个词曾指海星。

abstract.en: Picture a star that shifts against the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗相对其他星在挪动的星。

abstract.en: Imagine a belt of gravel circling the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈绕日的碎石带。

abstract.en: Think of a five-armed shape naming both sky and sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一个五臂形状同时给天空与海洋命名。

examples.en: The asteroid passes close to Earth next year.
examples.cn: 这颗小行星明年将近距离掠过地球。

examples.en: Scientists sampled the surface of an asteroid.
examples.cn: 科学家在一颗小行星表面取了样。

examples.en: An asteroid impact ended the dinosaurs.
examples.cn: 一次小行星撞击终结了恐龙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：aster「星」+ -oid「像……的」——看着像星其实在动的小石头，就是小行星 asteroid。

root: 希腊语 aster「星」加 eidos「形状」构成 asteroeides「像星的」；1802 年赫歇尔以此命名新发现的星点状天体，同根还有 aster、astral 与 astronomy。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name a shape, not a substance: a moving point of light in the sky, and a five-armed body on the seabed.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项命名的都是形状而非材质：天空中移动的光点，与海底五臂的躯体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a star-like point in the lens that slowly moves
core.cn: 核心意象：望远镜里一个像星点却会移动的小石头

branches.en: A point of light that shifts nightly.
A belt of gravel between two planets.
branches.cn: 两颗行星之间的碎石带。

branches.en: A five-armed body on a plate.
A shape shared by sky and sea.
branches.cn: 天空与海洋共用的形状。

branches.en: Named for looking like a star.

intro.en: Asteroid is aster- plus -oid; the star root also builds astronomy, astral and disaster, while -oid recurs in thyroid and meteoroid.
intro.cn: asteroid 是 aster- 加 -oid；「星」词根还构成 astronomy、astral 与 disaster，而 -oid 又出现在 thyroid 与 meteoroid 中。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek aster, star, matched by Latin astrum and stella; sidus, a constellation, gives sidereal.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 aster「星」，对应拉丁语 astrum 与 stella；sidus「星座」产生 sidereal。

definition_zh: n. 哮喘（气道慢性炎症，反复喘息、气短、胸闷）；由此产生的喘息状态
definition_en: A long-term condition in which the airways narrow and swell, causing repeated wheezing, coughing and breathlessness; also the resulting state of struggling to breathe.
core_image: 气道像被捏细的吸管，气进出都带着哨音
scene: 他一跑起来就喘，随身带着吸入器。Running brings on his asthma, so he carries an inhaler.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：asthma 指气道反复发炎变窄的慢性病，即哮喘。

senses.title: The long-term airway disease
senses.definition: a chronic condition in which the airways become inflamed and narrow, so breathing is repeatedly difficult
senses.definitionCN: 气道发炎变窄的慢性病，导致呼吸反复困难
senses.example: Her asthma is worse in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 她的哮喘在冷天更严重。
senses.why: The Greek root means to breathe hard, so the word names the effort of breathing rather than the lungs themselves.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「费力呼吸」，所以这个词命名的是呼吸的费力，而不是肺本身。

senses.title: The resulting struggle for breath
senses.definition: the state of wheezing and tightness at a given moment, as in his asthma is playing up
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻喘息与胸闷的状态，如「他的哮喘又闹起来了」
senses.example: The dust brought his asthma back within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘几分钟内就把他的喘息勾了回来。
senses.why: Speakers slide from the diagnosis to the present feeling, which is why the same noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 说话者会从诊断滑到当下的感受，所以同一个名词把两者都覆盖了。

intro.en: Asthma is Greek asthma, panting, from azein, to breathe hard, related to the verb for blowing that also gives aer, air.
intro.cn: asthma 就是希腊语 asthma「喘息」，出自 azein「费力呼吸」，与表示「吹」的动词同源，后者也给出 aer「空气」。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to blow or breathe lies behind words for air and for hard breathing.
items.cn: 一个意为「吹、呼吸」的拟构词根，藏在表示空气与费力呼吸的词背后。

items.en: Greek azein meant to breathe hard or pant, the physical effort the disease is named for.
items.cn: 希腊语 azein 意为「费力呼吸、喘」，正是这个病命名所依据的身体感受。

items.en: Greek asthma named panting itself, and physicians used it for the condition of laboured breathing.
items.cn: 希腊语 asthma 本指「喘息」，医生用它指呼吸费力的病症。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek term unchanged, and it travelled through medical Latin across Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样沿用了这个希腊词，它随医学拉丁语传遍欧洲。

items.en: English records asthma from the fourteenth century, long spelled with the th that is now silent.
items.cn: 英语从十四世纪起记录 asthma，长期保留如今不发音的 th 拼写。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine redefined it as chronic airway inflammation, which changed treatment from relief to control.
items.cn: 二十世纪医学把它重新定义为气道慢性炎症，使治疗从「缓解」转向「控制」。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against three words that only share the opening sound; the near-meaning group separates the symptom from neighbouring lung diseases.
note.cn: 形近组提醒不要与三个只是开头音相同的词混淆；近义组把症状与邻近的肺部疾病分开。

entries.definition: Affected by or relating to asthma.
entries.definitionCN: 患哮喘的；与哮喘有关的。

The wasting away of a body part.
Too few red cells in the blood.
To breathe with a whistling sound.
Inflammation of the larger airways.
Damage to the air sacs of the lungs.
The feeling of not getting enough air.

normalIntro.en: Asthma comes from a Greek verb for breathing hard, so the word names the effort, not the organ.
normalIntro.cn: asthma 出自一个表示「费力呼吸」的希腊动词，所以这个词命名的是「费力」，不是器官。

normal.en: The th is silent in both accents.
normal.cn: 两种口音里 th 都不发音。

normal.en: Asthmatic is the adjective and the person.
normal.cn: asthmatic 既是形容词也指患者。

normal.en: An asthma attack is one bout, not the disease.
normal.cn: an asthma attack 是一次发作，不是这个病。

normal.en: Asthma is uncountable, so no plural.
normal.cn: asthma 不可数，没有复数。

normal.en: Bronchitis and emphysema are different conditions.
normal.cn: bronchitis 与 emphysema 是不同的病。

abstract.en: Picture a drinking straw pinched in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一根中间被捏细的吸管。

abstract.en: Imagine a whistle sounding on every breath out.
abstract.cn: 想象每次呼气都响起一声哨音。

abstract.en: Think of an inhaler kept in a coat pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象外套口袋里常备的吸入器。

examples.en: Cold air can trigger asthma.
examples.cn: 冷空气可能诱发哮喘。

examples.en: He has managed his asthma for years.
examples.cn: 他多年来一直把哮喘控制得住。

examples.en: The clinic runs an asthma review each spring.
examples.cn: 这家门诊每年春天做一次哮喘复查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记忆：读作「阿兹玛」，想着「啊——嘶——」那口带哨音的气，就是哮喘 asthma（th 不发音）。

root: 希腊语 azein「费力呼吸」生出 asthma「喘息」，与 aer「空气」同源；拉丁语原样沿用，十四世纪入英语，拼写保留不发音的 th。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one narrow straw seen twice: the long-term diagnosis, and the whistling struggle of a particular moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一根被捏细的吸管被看了两遍：长期的诊断，以及某个时刻带哨音的挣扎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an airway pinched like a straw, every breath whistling
core.cn: 核心意象：气道像被捏细的吸管，气进出都带着哨音

branches.en: A chest tighter in cold weather.
A childhood diagnosis carried for life.
branches.cn: 从儿童期带到成年的诊断。
跑到一半伸手去拿吸入器。

branches.en: One narrowed straw, a diagnosis and a moment.
branches.cn: 同一根变窄的吸管，既是诊断也是一刻。

intro.en: Asthma takes the adjective ending -atic to give asthmatic; the surrounding lung vocabulary is built from bronch-, pneu- and -itis.
intro.cn: asthma 加形容词后缀 -atic 得 asthmatic；周边的肺部词汇由 bronch-、pneu- 与 -itis 搭起。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Latin spirare, to breathe, and spiritus, breath; Greek bronchos, windpipe, names the tube involved.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是拉丁语 spirare「呼吸」与 spiritus「气息」；希腊语 bronchos「气管」指发病时受累的那根管道。

latinEntries.exampleCN: spirare 产生 respire 与 inspire。

definition_en: to surprise someone very much, or to shock by something hard to believe
core_image: 一声雷在头顶炸开，人愣在原地
scene: 魔术师从帽子里变出一只活鸽子。The trick astonished the children.
sceneCN: 这里 astonish 是「使惊讶」（第 1 个义项：因意外而让人愣住）；句意是这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

pos.zh: 动词：使大为惊讶；使震惊

senses.title: Surprise greatly
senses.definition: to surprise someone very much by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 因出乎意料之事而让人极为惊讶
senses.example: The trick astonished the children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。
senses.why: Astonish goes back to Latin extonare, 'to strike with thunder', so the original picture is a person stunned by a clap overhead.
senses.whyCN: astonish 可追溯到拉丁语 extonare「雷击」，最初的画面就是人被头顶的一声雷震得愣住。

senses.title: Shock by something hard to believe
senses.definition: to shock someone with news or an event that seems unbelievable
senses.definitionCN: 用难以相信的消息或事件使人震惊
senses.example: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
senses.exampleCN: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。
senses.why: When the thunderbolt is bad news rather than a trick, the same stunned stillness reads as shock, which is why the word also covers disbelief at something grave.
senses.whyCN: 当那道雷不是戏法而是坏消息时，同样的僵住就成了一种震惊，所以这个词也能表示对严重事件的难以置信。

intro.en: Astonish is a thunder word: its ancestors describe being struck by lightning.
intro.cn: astonish 是个打雷的词，它的祖辈词描述被雷电击中。

items.en: tonare meant 'to thunder'.
items.cn: tonare 意为「打雷」。

items.en: extonare meant 'to strike with thunder'.
items.cn: extonare 意为「以雷击打」。

items.en: estoner meant 'to stun or amaze'.
items.cn: estoner 意为「震住、使惊愕」。

items.en: astonen meant 'to stun the mind'.
items.cn: astonen 意为「使心神震住」。

items.en: The spelling settled as astonish, with the thunder forgotten.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 astonish，打雷的画面渐渐被遗忘。

note.en: The look-alike group is the astonish family; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 astonish 词族；近义组是其他表示惊讶的动词。

entries.definition: great surprise
extremely surprising
to shock with surprise
to fill with wonder
to cause unexpected wonder

normalIntro.en: Think of a thunderclap that leaves a person standing still.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一声雷把人劈在原地不动。

normal.en: The subject is the startling thing, the object is the person.
normal.cn: 主语是令人吃惊的事物，宾语是人。

normal.en: The adjective astonishing describes the thing, astonished the person.
normal.cn: astonishing 形容事物，astonished 形容人。

normal.en: The noun is astonishment.
normal.cn: 名词是 astonishment。

normal.en: It is stronger than surprise.
normal.cn: 它比 surprise 程度更重。

normal.en: The middle syllable is stressed: as-TON-ish.
normal.cn: 重音在中间音节。

abstract.en: See a dove pulled from an empty hat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸽子从空帽子里被拎出来。

abstract.en: See a listener frozen with a cup halfway to the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象听的人僵住，杯子停在半空。

abstract.en: See a flash and then a room gone silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光之后，整个房间静下来。

examples.en: The trick astonished the children.
examples.cn: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

examples.en: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
examples.cn: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。

examples.en: She astonished us all by finishing first.
examples.cn: 她第一个完成，让我们都很吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词源里藏着「雷」：拉丁语 extonare 是被雷击中。人被雷劈中般僵住，就是大为惊讶；遇到难以相信的坏消息，就是震惊。

root: 源自拉丁语 extonare「以雷击打」，由 ex- 加强语气与 tonare「打雷」构成，经古法语 estoner 进入英语；由「被雷震住」引申为大为惊讶与震惊。

sensesIntro.en: A wonderful trick and a terrible scale of damage can both freeze a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 精彩的戏法与骇人的损失规模，都能让人僵在原地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thunderclap directly overhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶炸开的一声雷。

intro.en: The word carries a hidden thunder root, ton, visible also in detonate.
intro.cn: 这个词藏着表示「雷」的词根 ton，在 detonate 里也能看到。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonare, 'to thunder', and its compounds entered English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonare「打雷」及其复合词经法语进入英语。

definition_en: to shock someone deeply with something unexpected
core_image: 一声雷在头顶炸开，全场的人张大了嘴
scene: 礼堂的灯亮起，幕布拉开，评委席上没有人料到下一秒的歌声。The singer's final high note would astound the entire panel.
sceneCN: 这里 astound 是「使震惊」（第 1 个义项：因意外而深深震撼）；句意为歌手最后的高音将令全体评委震惊。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人震惊的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「惊人地」
同族近形词，义为「使惊讶」

senses.title: To shock with the unexpected
senses.definition: to overwhelm someone with sudden surprise
senses.definitionCN: 以突来的意外彻底震住某人
senses.example: The verdict astounded the courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 判决令整个法庭愕然。
senses.why: The Latin root ex-tonare means to thunder out; the shock lands like thunder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 ex-tonare 意为雷声炸响；震惊正如惊雷落地。

senses.title: To overwhelm with wonder
senses.definition: to fill someone with amazed admiration
senses.definitionCN: 以惊叹与叹服充满内心
senses.example: The acrobats astounded everyone with their balance.
senses.exampleCN: 杂技演员的平衡技令所有人叹服。
senses.why: Thunder becomes awe when the surprise is also splendid.
senses.whyCN: 当意外同时精彩绝伦，惊雷便化作惊叹。

intro.en: Astound arose in English around the seventeenth century, blending astonish and stun, both from Latin ex-tonare, to thunder out.
intro.cn: astound 约于十七世纪在英语中出现，混合了 astonish 与 stun，二者均源自拉丁语 ex-tonare（如雷声般炸响）。

items.en: The root *(s)ten- meant to thunder or resound.
items.cn: 词根 *(s)ten- 意为打雷、轰鸣。

items.en: Extontanare meant to thunder out, to stun.
items.cn: 拉丁语 extontanare 意为如雷炸响、令人失神。

items.en: Estoner passed into English as astonish.
items.cn: 古法语 estoner 进入英语成为 astonish。

items.en: Stun developed as a native short form of the thunder idea.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语中 stun 发展为「雷击般失神」的简短形式。

items.en: Astound blended the two, first as a past participle, then a full verb.
items.cn: 十七世纪 astound 由二者混合而成，先作过去分词，后成完整动词。

note.en: Astound fuses astonish and stun: thunder written twice over.
note.cn: astound 融合 astonish 与 stun：同一声惊雷写了两遍。

entries.definition: to surprise greatly, slightly milder
to daze with a blow or shock
entries.definitionCN: 使目瞪口呆（同根短形式）

entries.definition: shockingly impressive
similar shape, means to be plentiful, different root
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在（形近，词源不同）

entries.definition: as if struck by lightning with surprise
entries.definitionCN: 如遭雷击般震惊（同意象合成词）

entries.definition: to upset with sudden bad news
to overwhelm with shock
to surprise utterly
to leave someone speechless
to fill with wonder

normalIntro.en: Read astound as a-STUN-d: a stun so strong it adds a thunder clap.
normalIntro.cn: 把 astound 读作 a-STUN-d：在 stun 之上再加一声惊雷。

normal.en: blend of astonish and stun.
normal.cn: 由 astonish 与 stun 混合而成。

normal.en: tonare means thunder, as in detonate.
normal.cn: tonare 意为打雷，如 detonate。

normal.en: astonish is the milder sibling.
normal.cn: astonish 是较温和的兄弟词。

normal.en: astounding describes shocking facts.
normal.cn: astounding 形容惊人的事实。

normal.en: usually a strong, positive or dramatic surprise.
normal.cn: 通常指强烈或戏剧性的意外。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom gasping at a verdict.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭因判决而集体倒吸凉气。

abstract.en: Hear one huge drumbeat in silence.
abstract.cn: 听寂静中响起一声巨鼓。

abstract.en: Feel the floor drop from under your certainties.
abstract.cn: 体会脚下的笃定忽然塌陷。

examples.en: The magician's escape astounded the police.
examples.cn: 魔术师的脱身令警察惊愕。

examples.en: Sales figures astounded the board.
examples.cn: 销售数字令董事会震惊。

examples.en: She astounded her teachers with fluent Greek.
examples.cn: 她流利的希腊语令老师们惊叹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额死淘的」——消息一来额吓得死淘（跌坐）在地，即 astound 之震惊。

root: 拉丁语 ex-tonare（雷声炸响）→ 古法语 estoner → 英语 astonish 与本土 stun → 十七世纪混合为 astound（使震惊）。

sensesIntro.en: One thunder image grows into shock and into amazed admiration.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一声惊雷，既炸出惊愕，也炸出叹服。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thunderclap in a silent hall
core.cn: 核心意象：寂静礼堂里的一声惊雷

branches.en: stunning with bad or huge news

intro.en: The thunder root shows shock as a blow of sound.
intro.cn: 雷声词根把震惊表现为一声巨响的打击。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonare, to thunder, powers astonish, stun and astound alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonare（打雷）同时驱动 astonish、stun 与 astound。
